newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus cuts refinancing rate to 38 pct vs 42 pct.
newsitem.headline: Belarus cuts refinancing rate to 38 pct vs 42 pct.

text.p: The Belarus central bank said on Tuesday it would cut its refinancing rate to 38 percent from 42 percent, effective Wednesday.
The central bank said in a statement the move was linked to the "significant lowering of the rate of inflation and devaluation of the Belarussian rouble."
The Statistics Ministry said July inflation slowed to 1.4 percent from June's 4.5 percent.

But first-half inflation was 41.7 percent against 21 percent in the same 1996 period. The International Monetary Fund recently recommended the former Soviet republic raise its refinancing rate due to growing inflation.
Belarus last changed the refinancing rate in February, when it raised it to 42 percent from 35 percent.
